resources.string: This device does not share the hotspot state with apps. Connect Shizuku or check it in Android settings.
No app on this device can open this.
Android does not let apps turn the hotspot on or off, read its password or change its settings. With Shizuku, Able can do it and then checks the real result. Without it, use Android settings.

Able uses Shizuku to call the same Android services that the Settings app uses (tethering and Wi-Fi). These are not public Android APIs: some options may be missing or behave differently on some devices or Android versions, and Able reports when that happens. You can revoke Shizuku access at any time in the Shizuku app.
Connect Shizuku to control the hotspot from Able.

Shares the network name and password as text (WIFI: format) with the app you choose. Anyone who receives it can join your hotspot. Change the password to revoke access.

Changes are saved in Android\'s hotspot settings, the same ones used by the Settings app. After applying, Able reads the settings back and shows the real values. Changing the name, password, security, band or visibility restarts a running hotspot.

Changing the security type or password disconnects every connected device; they must join again with the new password. WPA3 is more secure but older devices may not connect; WPA2/WPA3 accepts both. An open network lets anyone nearby use your connection.

5 GHz is faster but has shorter range; Android falls back to 2.4 GHz when 5 GHz cannot be used (for example in some countries or while connected to Wi-Fi). 6 GHz needs WPA3 and a compatible device. Changing the band restarts a running hotspot.
Anyone nearby can connect and use your mobile data.
To apply these changes Android restarts the hotspot. Every connected device is disconnected and must join again (with the new password, if you changed it).
